1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_i2c1.c
3:  *
4:  * Interrupt-driven hardware I2C1 master-write driver.  See
5:  * include/bk7258_i2c1.h for the full rationale (why this board needs
6:  * hardware I2C1 on GPIO42/43 instead of the previous bk7258_i2c_sim.c
7:  * bit-banged GPIO0/1 driver).
8:  *
9:  * State machine and register-access sequencing are a from-scratch
10:  * reimplementation of bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
11:  * ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c's I2C_MASTER_WRITE path
12:  * (i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl() -> i2c_master_start() ->
13:  * i2c_master_set_write_dev_addr() -> i2c_master_write_mem_addr_low_8bit()
14:  * -> i2c1_master_write_data() -> i2c_master_stop()), driven by
15:  * i2c1_isr_common()'s per-byte-ACK interrupt handling.  Register bit
16:  * layout: hardware/bk7258_i2c1.h (ported from that release's
17:  * i2c_struct.h/i2c_reg.h).
18:  *
19:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
20:  ****************************************************************************/
21: 
22: #include <nuttx/config.h>
23: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
24: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
25: #include <nuttx/semaphore.h>
26: #include <nuttx/spinlock.h>
27: #include <stdbool.h>
28: #include <stdint.h>
29: #include <stdio.h>
30: 
31: #include "arm_internal.h"
32: #include "irq.h"
33: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
34: #include "bk7258_i2c1.h"
35: #include "hardware/bk7258_i2c1.h"
36: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
37: 
38: /* GPIO42/GPIO43 pinmux function index for I2C1_SCL/I2C1_SDA.
39:  *
40:  * bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h's per-pin
41:  * function array for GPIO_42 is:
42:  *   {GPIO_DEV_I2C1_SCL, GPIO_DEV_I2S2_DIN, GPIO_DEV_LIN_SLEEP,
43:  *    GPIO_DEV_SCR_RSTN, GPIO_DEV_LCD_G2, GPIO_DEV_DEBUG30,
44:  *    GPIO_DEV_INVALID, GPIO_DEV_SLCD_SEG1}
45:  * i.e. GPIO_DEV_I2C1_SCL is array index 0.  GPIO_43's array is the same
46:  * shape with GPIO_DEV_I2C1_SDA at index 0.  bk7258_gpio_set_function()'s
47:  * "function" parameter is this array index (see bk7258_gpio.c: it writes
48:  * `function & 0xf` into the 4-bit-per-pin GPIO_SYS_CFG pinmux-select
49:  * field). */
50: #define BK7258_I2C1_SCL_PIN       42u
51: #define BK7258_I2C1_SDA_PIN       43u
52: #define BK7258_I2C1_PINMUX_FUNCTION 0u
53: 
54: /* 100kHz standard-mode I2C, matching GC2145's supported bus speed and
55:  * gsensor_sc7a20.c's i2c_cfg.baud_rate=100000 convention for this SoC
56:  * family. */
57: #define BK7258_I2C1_BAUD_RATE     100000u
58: 
59: /* freq_div formula: bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/i2c_hal.c
60:  * I2C_CLK_DIVID(rate) = ROUND_UP(ROUND_UP(CONFIG_XTAL_FREQ, rate) - 6, 3)
61:  * - 1.  CONFIG_XTAL_FREQ for this board's 26MHz crystal (schematic sheet
62:  * 2/6, "26M,12pF,85C" crystal note) is 26000000. */
63: #define BK7258_I2C1_XTAL_FREQ     26000000u
64: #define BK7258_I2C1_ROUND_UP(a, b) (((a) / (b)) + (((a) % (b)) ? 1u : 0u))
65: #define BK7258_I2C1_FREQ_DIV(rate) \
66:   (BK7258_I2C1_ROUND_UP(BK7258_I2C1_ROUND_UP(BK7258_I2C1_XTAL_FREQ, (rate)) - 6u, 3u) - 1u)
67: 
68: /* Master-write state sequence, mirroring i2c_driver.c's
69:  * i2c_master_status_t (only the subset this write-only driver needs). */
70: enum bk7258_i2c1_state_e
71: {
72:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE = 0,
73:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR,
74:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_REG_ADDR,
75:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DATA,
76: };
77: 
78: static sem_t g_i2c1_done_sem;
79: static volatile enum bk7258_i2c1_state_e g_i2c1_state;
80: static volatile bool g_i2c1_ack_ok;
81: static uint8_t g_i2c1_dev_addr;
82: static uint8_t g_i2c1_reg_addr;
83: static uint8_t g_i2c1_data;
84: 
85: static void bk7258_i2c1_stop(void)
86: {
87:   /* Per i2c_ll_enable_stop()'s comment in the reference driver: sm_int
88:    * (bit[0]) and stop (bit[9]) must be written together in the same
89:    * write, otherwise the hardware will not actually issue a STOP
90:    * condition on the bus. */
91:   putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT | BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_STOP,
92:            BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
93:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
94: }
95: 
96: static int bk7258_i2c1_isr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
97: {
98:   uint32_t int_status = getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
99: 
100:   if ((int_status & BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT) == 0)
101:     {
102:       /* Not the per-byte state-machine interrupt (e.g. scl_timeout,
103:        * arb_lost): clear whatever fired and bail out without touching
104:        * the write sequence, matching i2c1_isr_common()'s early return
105:        * for the same condition. */
106:       putreg32(int_status, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
107:       return 0;
108:     }
109: 
110:   /* ack (bit[8]) reads as 1 when the previous byte was ACKed by the
111:    * slave, per i2c_ll_is_rx_ack_triggered()/i2c_ll_is_tx_ack_triggered()
112:    * both testing BIT(8) -- the same status bit serves both roles
113:    * depending on tx_mode, which master-write transactions always are. */
114:   bool acked = (int_status & BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_ACK) != 0;
115: 
116:   if (!acked)
117:     {
118:       g_i2c1_ack_ok = false;
119:       bk7258_i2c1_stop();
120:       nxsem_post(&g_i2c1_done_sem);
121:       /* Clear the interrupt (sm_int alone; no stop/start bit needed here
122:        * since bk7258_i2c1_stop() already issued its own combined
123:        * sm_int|stop write above). */
124:       putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
125:       return 0;
126:     }
127: 
128:   switch (g_i2c1_state)
129:     {
130:       case BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR:
131:         g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_REG_ADDR;
132:         putreg32(g_i2c1_reg_addr & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
133:                  BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
134:         putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
135:         break;
136: 
137:       case BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_REG_ADDR:
138:         g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DATA;
139:         putreg32(g_i2c1_data & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
140:                  BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
141:         putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
142:         break;
143: 
144:       case BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DATA:
145:         g_i2c1_ack_ok = true;
146:         bk7258_i2c1_stop();
147:         nxsem_post(&g_i2c1_done_sem);
148:         putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
149:         break;
150: 
151:       default:
152:         putreg32(int_status, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
153:         break;
154:     }
155: 
156:   return 0;
157: }
158: 
159: void bk7258_i2c1_init(void)
160: {
161:   uint32_t freq_div = BK7258_I2C1_FREQ_DIV(BK7258_I2C1_BAUD_RATE);
162: 
163:   nxsem_init(&g_i2c1_done_sem, 0, 0);
164:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
165: 
166:   /* Enable the I2C1 *module* clock gate (BK_avdk_smp's
167:    * sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up(CLK_PWR_ID_I2C2, ...), called from
168:    * i2c_clock_enable(I2C_ID_1) in the reference i2c_driver.c).  This is
169:    * a separate, more fundamental gate than sm_bus_cfg.freq_div (the bus
170:    * baud-rate divider) or global_ctrl.clk_gate_bypass (an internal
171:    * ack-bit-visibility bypass): without this bit, the I2C1 block's
172:    * state machine receives no clock at all, so writing the start bit
173:    * in bk7258_i2c1_write_reg() is accepted by the register interface
174:    * (which is on a different, always-clocked bus) but never actually
175:    * advances the transaction -- sm_int never fires, indistinguishable
176:    * from a dead bus purely from register-level symptoms.  See
177:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_I2C1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
178:    * the register-map citation. */
179:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0, BK7258_I2C1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
180: 
181:   /* Route GPIO42/GPIO43 to the I2C1_SCL/I2C1_SDA hardware function.
182:    *
183:    * NOTE: bk7258_gpio_input_pullup() must NOT be called here (as an
184:    * earlier version of this driver did, attempting to also enable the
185:    * pins' internal pull-ups): it unconditionally clears
186:    * BK7258_GPIO_SECOND_FUNCTION (see bk7258_gpio.c), and
187:    * bk7258_gpio_set_function() unconditionally clears
188:    * BK7258_GPIO_PULL_ENABLE (see the same file) -- calling both back to
189:    * back, in either order, leaves one of "second function selected" or
190:    * "internal pull-up enabled" clobbered by the other's write.  This
191:    * board's schematic (sheet 4/6) already provides external 4.7K
192:    * pull-ups to VDDGPIO on both IIC1_SCL/IIC1_SDA nets, so the internal
193:    * pull-up is not required for correct bus operation; only the pinmux
194:    * function selection matters here. */
195:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(BK7258_I2C1_SCL_PIN, BK7258_I2C1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
196:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(BK7258_I2C1_SDA_PIN, BK7258_I2C1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
197: 
198:   /* Soft-reset then configure sm_bus_cfg, matching i2c_hal_init_instance()
199:    * (soft_reset=1, then zero sm_bus_cfg/sm_bus_status) followed by
200:    * i2c_hal_configure()'s field-by-field setup. */
201:   putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SOFT_RESET, BK7258_I2C1_GLOBAL_CTRL);
202:   putreg32(0, BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG);
203:   putreg32(0, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
204: 
205:   putreg32((freq_div << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_FREQ_DIV_SHIFT) &
206:            BK7258_I2C1_CFG_FREQ_DIV_MASK,
207:            BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG);
208: 
209:   /* idle_cr=0x3, scl_cr=0x4, clk_src=0x3, timeout_en=1, idle_det_en=1,
210:    * inh=0 (i2c_ll_enable_slave() clears inh to 0 even though this driver
211:    * never acts as a slave, matching i2c_hal_configure()'s call order:
212:    * enable_slave() runs after the cr/clk_src/timeout/idle_det writes). */
213:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG,
214:               BK7258_I2C1_CFG_IDLE_CR_MASK | BK7258_I2C1_CFG_SCL_CR_MASK |
215:               BK7258_I2C1_CFG_CLK_SRC_MASK,
216:               (0x3u << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_IDLE_CR_SHIFT) |
217:               (0x4u << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_SCL_CR_SHIFT) |
218:               (0x3u << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_CLK_SRC_SHIFT));
219:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_INH,
220:               BK7258_I2C1_CFG_TIMEOUT_EN | BK7258_I2C1_CFG_IDLE_DET_EN);
221: 
222:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_I2C1, bk7258_i2c1_isr, NULL);
223:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_I2C1);
224: 
225:   /* Enable the peripheral (sm_bus_cfg.en=1), also bypassing the clock
226:    * gate so the ack bit is actually readable in the ISR -- per
227:    * i2c_ll_enable()'s comment: "need open clock bypass, otherwise cannot
228:    * read ack(BIT8) in i2c_isr". */
229:   putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_CLK_GATE_BYPASS, BK7258_I2C1_GLOBAL_CTRL);
230:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, 0, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN);
231: }
232: 
233: bool bk7258_i2c1_write_reg(uint8_t i2c_addr, uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
234: {
235:   irqstate_t flags;
236:   int ret;
237:   int busy_wait_us;
238: 
239:   /* Wait for the bus to report idle before issuing a new START,
240:    * matching i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl()'s
241:    * i2c_wait_sm_bus_idle() call.  sm_bus_status.busy (bit[15]) lives in
242:    * the same register as INT_STATUS (both are REG_0x05 per
243:    * i2c_struct.h's sm_bus_status union), so BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS is
244:    * read here rather than a separate "status" register.  Without this
245:    * check, if busy is stuck set (e.g. right after
246:    * bk7258_i2c1_init() enables the peripheral while the external bus
247:    * lines are still settling), writing the start bit below would be
248:    * silently ignored by the hardware state machine -- producing
249:    * exactly the "interrupt never fires, write_reg() times out"
250:    * symptom, indistinguishable from a dead/unwired bus without this
251:    * check to rule it out. */
252:   for (busy_wait_us = 0;
253:        (getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS) &
254:         BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_BUSY) != 0 && busy_wait_us < 10000;
255:        busy_wait_us += 100)
256:     {
257:       up_udelay(100);
258:     }
259: 
260:   g_i2c1_dev_addr = i2c_addr;
261:   g_i2c1_reg_addr = reg;
262:   g_i2c1_data = value;
263:   g_i2c1_ack_ok = false;
264: 
265:   flags = enter_critical_section();
266: 
267:   /* Write the (7-bit addr << 1 | write-bit=0) byte first, then set
268:    * start=1, matching i2c_master_set_write_dev_addr()'s comment: "write
269:    * slave_addr first, then enable start bit, otherwise the slave_addr
270:    * written will be zero." */
271:   putreg32((uint32_t)(i2c_addr << 1) & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
272:            BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
273:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR;
274:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS, 0, BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START);
275: 
276:   leave_critical_section(flags);
277: 
278:   /* Bounded wait: 100ms is generous for a 3-byte 100kHz transaction
279:    * (~270us of bus time) plus scheduling jitter, while still failing
280:    * fast if the slave never responds (e.g. wrong wiring) rather than
281:    * hanging board_late_initialize() indefinitely. */
282:   ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_i2c1_done_sem, MSEC2TICK(100));
283:   if (ret < 0)
284:     {
285:       /* Timed out: the ISR never ran to completion (either the I2C1
286:        * interrupt never fired at all -- e.g. pinmux/clock
287:        * misconfiguration, or a hardware issue independent of ACK/NACK
288:        * -- or it fired but got stuck mid-sequence).  This is a
289:        * distinct failure mode from a clean NACK (which nxsem_post()s
290:        * promptly with g_i2c1_ack_ok=false) and is logged differently
291:        * here so board bring-up logs can tell "the bus electrically
292:        * never responded at all" apart from "the slave was reachable
293:        * and explicitly rejected". */
294:       printf("i2c1: write_reg(addr=0x%02x, reg=0x%02x) timed out "
295:              "waiting for the I2C1 interrupt (int_status=0x%08x, "
296:              "sm_bus_cfg=0x%08x) -- the ISR never completed the "
297:              "transaction\n",
298:              i2c_addr, reg, (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS),
299:              (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG));
300: 
301:       /* Timed out: force the state machine back to idle so the next
302:        * write_reg() call starts clean, and disable+re-enable the
303:        * peripheral to clear any stuck bus condition, matching
304:        * i2c1_isr_common()'s SCL-timeout recovery path
305:        * (i2c_hal_disable() + i2c_hal_enable()). */
306:       g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
307:       modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN, 0);
308:       modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, 0, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN);
309:       return false;
310:     }
311: 
312:   if (!g_i2c1_ack_ok)
313:     {
314:       printf("i2c1: write_reg(addr=0x%02x, reg=0x%02x) got a clean "
315:              "NACK (the I2C1 interrupt fired and completed, but the "
316:              "slave never pulled ACK) -- the bus is electrically "
317:              "responsive, the device at this address is not\n",
318:              i2c_addr, reg);
319:     }
320: 
321:   return g_i2c1_ack_ok;
322: }

5: #ifndef __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_HARDWARE_BK7258_I2C1_H
6: #define __VENDOR_BEKEN_CHIPS_BK7258_HARDWARE_BK7258_I2C1_H

8: #include <stdint.h>

10: #include "bk7258_memorymap.h"
11: 
12: /* Register layout per bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
13:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/i2c_struct.h (i2c_typedef_t) and
14:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/i2c_reg.h.  Each I2C unit (I2C0 at
15:  * SOC_I2C0_REG_BASE, I2C1 at SOC_I2C1_REG_BASE) has an identical 8-word
16:  * register block; this board only wires up I2C1 (BK7258_I2C1_BASE), so
17:  * only that block's offsets are defined here. */
18: 
19: #define BK7258_I2C1_DEV_ID          (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x00u)
20: #define BK7258_I2C1_DEV_VERSION     (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x04u)
21: #define BK7258_I2C1_GLOBAL_CTRL     (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x08u)
22: #define BK7258_I2C1_DEV_STATUS      (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x0cu)
23: #define BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG      (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x10u)
24: #define BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS      (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x14u)
25: #define BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA     (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x18u)
26: #define BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_EX_CFG   (BK7258_I2C1_BASE + 0x1cu)
27: 
28: /* global_ctrl (REG_0x02) */
29: #define BK7258_I2C1_SOFT_RESET       (1u << 0)
30: #define BK7258_I2C1_CLK_GATE_BYPASS  (1u << 1)
31: 
32: /* sm_bus_cfg (REG_0x04) */

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_i2c1.h
3:  *
4:  * Interrupt-driven hardware I2C1 master driver.
5:  *
6:  * This replaces the earlier software-simulated (bit-banged) I2C driver
7:  * (bk7258_i2c_sim.c/.h) for GC2145 camera register access.  The switch
8:  * was forced by the board schematic (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf, sheet
9:  * 4/6 "DVP/SENSOR/NAND/MOTOR/KEY"), which shows GC2145's SCL/SDA wired to
10:  * the chip's *hardware* I2C1 peripheral (network labels IIC1_SCL/
11:  * IIC1_SDA, with 4.7K pull-ups to VDDGPIO) -- not to a pair of plain
12:  * GPIOs that firmware could bit-bang arbitrarily.  The previous driver's
13:  * choice of GPIO0/GPIO1 for bit-banging was based on a reference
14:  * project's default config (bk_avdk_smp dvp_example) that does not match
15:  * this board: GPIO0/GPIO1 are actually wired to UART1_TXD/UART1_RXD here
16:  * (schematic sheet 2/6 pin table), which explains why every prior
17:  * hardware bring-up attempt saw the GC2145 never ACK the first I2C byte
18:  * -- the bit-banged signal was toggling the wrong physical pins.
19:  *
20:  * The real IIC1_SCL/IIC1_SDA nets are routed by the chip's pinmux to
21:  * GPIO42/GPIO43 (bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h
22:  * GPIO_I2C1_MAP_TABLE's second entry, BIT64(42)|BIT64(43); the first
23:  * entry, GPIO0/GPIO1, is I2C1's *other* selectable pin group used by a
24:  * different board, not this one).  This driver hard-codes GPIO42/43 as
25:  * this board's only wiring; it is not a general-purpose pinmux-selectable
26:  * I2C1 driver.
27:  *
28:  * Architecture: this is a from-scratch reimplementation of the interrupt
29:  * + semaphore master state machine in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
30:  * ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c (i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl(),
31:  * i2c_master_isr_common(), i2c1_isr_common()), adapted to NuttX's
32:  * irq_attach()/up_enable_irq()/nxsem_wait() primitives in place of
33:  * Beken RTOS's bk_int_isr_register()/rtos_get_semaphore().  Only the
34:  * master-write path is implemented (I2C_MASTER_WRITE state sequence:
35:  * START -> TX_DEV_ADDR -> TX_MEM_ADDR -> TX_DATA -> STOP); master-read,
36:  * slave mode, 10-bit addressing, and low-power-sleep register
37:  * backup/restore are intentionally omitted, since GC2145 bring-up (585 +
38:  * 40 register writes, all 8-bit register address / 8-bit data, no
39:  * readback) is this driver's only consumer.
40:  */

407: static bk_err_t i2c1_master_write_data(i2c_id_t id)
408: {
409: 	uint32_t data_size = 0;
410: 	uint32_t remain_size = s_i2c[id].data_size - s_i2c[id].data_offset;
411: 	if (!remain_size) {
412: 		I2C_LOGV("data_size:%d tx done\r\n", s_i2c[id].data_size);
413: 		i2c_master_stop(id);
414: 		rtos_set_semaphore(&s_i2c[id].tx_sema);
415: 		return BK_OK;
416: 	}
417: 	uint32_t empty_fifo_num = i2c_hal_get_write_empty_fifo_num(&s_i2c[id].hal);
418: 	if (remain_size < empty_fifo_num) {
419: 		data_size = remain_size;
420: 	} else {
421: 		data_size = empty_fifo_num;
422: 	}
423: 	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < data_size; i++) {
424: 		i2c_master_write_byte(id, s_i2c[id].data_ptr[(s_i2c[id].data_offset)++]);
425: 	}
426: 	remain_size = s_i2c[id].data_size - s_i2c[id].data_offset;
427: 	if (remain_size < empty_fifo_num) {
428: 		I2C_LOGV("remain_size:%d, empty_fifo_num:%d\r\n", remain_size, empty_fifo_num);
429: 		s_i2c[id].int_status &= ~(I2C1_F_INT_MODE_V | I2C1_F_START);
430: 	}

435: bk_err_t i2c1_master_read_data(i2c_id_t id)
436: {

438: 		I2C_LOGV("master_read i2c_is_start\r\n");
439: 		s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_ACK;
440: 		s_i2c[id].master_status = I2C_RX_DATA;
441: 		return BK_OK;
442: 	}
443: 	uint32_t fifo_num = i2c_hal_get_read_fifo_num(&s_i2c[id].hal);
444: 	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < fifo_num; i++) {
445: 		s_i2c[id].data_ptr[(s_i2c[id].data_offset)++] = i2c_hal_read_byte(&s_i2c[id].hal);
446: 		if (s_i2c[id].data_offset == s_i2c[id].data_size) { /* avoid index is out of array range */
447: 			break;
448: 		}
449: 	}
450: 	uint32_t remain_size = s_i2c[id].data_size - s_i2c[id].data_offset;
451: 	if (!remain_size) {
452: 		s_i2c[id].int_status &= ~(I2C1_F_ACK | I2C1_F_START);
453: 		i2c_master_stop(id);
454: 		rtos_set_semaphore(&s_i2c[id].rx_sema);
455: 	} else if (remain_size < fifo_num) {
456: 		s_i2c[id].int_status |= (I2C1_F_ACK | I2C1_F_INT_MODE_V);
457: 		s_i2c[id].master_status = I2C_RX_DATA;
458: 	} else {
459: 		s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_ACK;
460: 		s_i2c[id].master_status = I2C_RX_DATA;
461: 	}
462: 	return BK_OK;
463: }

1038: 			i2c_transtate_set(id);
1039: 			i2c_master_stop(id);
1040: 			s_i2c[id].err_code = BK_ERR_I2C_ACK_TIMEOUT;
1041: 			rtos_set_semaphore(&s_i2c[id].tx_sema);
1042: 			break;
1043: 		}
1044: 		i2c_master_isr_common(id);
1045: 		break;
1046: 	}
1047: 
1048: 	case I2C_MASTER_READ: {
1049: 		s_i2c[id].int_status &= ~I2C1_F_START;
1050: 		if (i2c_hal_is_start_triggered(hal, int_status) &&
1051: 			!i2c_hal_is_rx_ack_triggered(hal, int_status)) {
1052: 			I2C_LOGW("i2c(%d) master_read get ack failed\r\n", id);
1053: 			s_i2c[id].master_status = I2C_IDLE;
1054: 			s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_STOP;
1055: 			s_i2c[id].err_code = BK_ERR_I2C_ACK_TIMEOUT;
1056: 			rtos_set_semaphore(&s_i2c[id].rx_sema);
1057: 			break;
1058: 		}
1059: 		i2c_master_isr_common(id);
1060: 		break;
1061: 	}
1062: 
1063: 	case I2C_SLAVE_WRITE:
1064: 		if (i2c_hal_is_stop_triggered(hal, int_status) || i2c_hal_is_rx_mode(hal)) {
1065: 			I2C_LOGD("i2c(%d) slave_write get stopped\r\n", id);
1066: 			rtos_set_semaphore(&s_i2c[id].tx_sema);
1067: 			break;
1068: 		}
1069: 		if (i2c_hal_is_addr_matched(hal)) {
1070: 			s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_ACK;
1071: 		}
1072: 
1073: 		i2c_hal_write_byte(hal, s_i2c[id].data_ptr[(s_i2c[id].data_offset)++]);
1074: 		if (s_i2c[id].data_offset == s_i2c[id].data_size) {
1075: 			I2C_LOGV("i2c(%d) slave_write data_offset==data_size\r\n", id);
1076: 		}
1077: 
1078: 		break;
1079: 
1080: 	case I2C_SLAVE_READ:
1081: 		if (i2c_hal_is_stop_triggered(hal, int_status)) {
1082: 			I2C_LOGD("i2c(%d) slave_read get stopped\r\n", id);
1083: 			rtos_set_semaphore(&s_i2c[id].rx_sema);
1084: 			break;
1085: 		}
1086: 		if (i2c_hal_is_addr_matched(hal)) {
1087: 			s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_ACK;
1088: 			break;
1089: 		}
1090: 		remain_size = s_i2c[id].data_size - s_i2c[id].data_offset;
1091: 		data_num = i2c_hal_get_read_fifo_num(hal);
1092: 		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < data_num; i++) {
1093: 			s_i2c[id].data_ptr[(s_i2c[id].data_offset)++] = i2c_hal_read_byte(hal);
1094: 			remain_size--;
1095: 			if (!remain_size) { /* avoid index is out of array range */
1096: 				break;
1097: 			}
1098: 		}
1099: 		if (!remain_size) {
1100: 			s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_ACK;
1101: 		} else if (remain_size < data_num) {
1102: 			s_i2c[id].int_status |= (I2C1_F_ACK | I2C1_F_INT_MODE_V);
1103: 		} else {
1104: 			s_i2c[id].int_status |= I2C1_F_ACK;
1105: 		}
1106: 		break;
1107: 
1108: 	default:
1109: 		break;
1110: 	}
1111: 	/* int_status sm_int/ack/start/stop/int_mode must operate together, otherwise will not work
1112: 	 * e.g.
1113: 	 * i2c_hal_enable_ack();  // only set bit of ack(bit[8]), no ack will be sent
1114: 	 */
1115: 	i2c_hal_clear_interrupt_status(hal, s_i2c[id].int_status);
1116: }

2:  * board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/sim_tests_gc2145/test_gc2145.c
3:  *
4:  * Integration test for bk7258_gc2145.c, compiled against the real
5:  * production source (unmodified) plus the real bk7258_gpio.c/
6:  * bk7258_i2c1.c/bk7258_dma.c/bk7258_yuv_buf.c drivers, using the same
7:  * mock register/IRQ infrastructure as board/beken/chips/bk7258/
8:  * sim_tests/.
9:  *
10:  * Mock I2C1 slave design: unlike the earlier bit-banged bk7258_i2c_sim.c
11:  * driver (which this test previously modeled at the GPIO SCL/SDA pin
12:  * level, reconstructing clock edges from raw register writes), the
13:  * hardware I2C1 controller exposes a byte-at-a-time register interface
14:  * (sm_bus_data for the byte being transferred, sm_bus_status.ack for the
15:  * per-byte ACK/NACK result) -- there is no bit-level bus to simulate.
16:  * This mock therefore tracks transaction state (address byte -> register
17:  * byte -> data byte -> STOP) purely from writes to BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA
18:  * and BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS's start/stop bits, and drives the ack bit in
19:  * BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS accordingly before synchronously firing the I2C1
20:  * ISR -- mirroring how a real slave's ACK would be visible to the
21:  * hardware state machine by the time the sm_int interrupt fires.
22:  *
23:  * Firing the ISR synchronously from the write hook (rather than from a
24:  * separate simulated interrupt source) is what makes this mock work in
25:  * a single-threaded test process with no real scheduler: by the time
26:  * bk7258_i2c1_write_reg() reaches nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(), the
27:  * whole START->address->register->data->STOP sequence has already run
28:  * to completion (recursively, from inside the initial start-bit write
29:  * that kicks it off) and nxsem_post() has already incremented the
30:  * semaphore count sim_stubs.c's mock checks.
31:  *
32:  * The line-done interrupt wait loop in bk7258_gc2145_test() is a
33:  * blocking busy-wait with no real asynchrony in this single-threaded
34:  * test process (up_udelay() is a no-op stub, and there is no timer
35:  * thread to fire bk7258_sim_irq_fire() *during* the wait).  This test
36:  * therefore pre-arms the mock YUV_BUF/DMA interrupt state *before*
37:  * calling bk7258_gc2145_test(), using a write hook on the YUV_BUF start
38:  * register (ctrl.yuv_mode) to fire the line-done interrupt synchronously
39:  * the moment the driver calls bk7258_yuv_buf_start() -- and another hook
40:  * on the DMA ctrl register to fire the DMA-done interrupt synchronously
41:  * the moment the driver calls bk7258_dma_start() -- so by the time
42:  * either wait loop's *first* condition check runs, the flag it is
43:  * waiting on is already set.  This validates the exact same call
44:  * sequence and control flow the real driver uses, without needing to
45:  * modify bk7258_gc2145.c to be testable or spin up real threads.

48:  ****************************************************************************/

92: /* ========================================================================
93:  * Mock I2C1 hardware slave: tracks the master-write byte sequence via
94:  * BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA writes and BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS's start bit,
95:  * and synchronously fires the I2C1 ISR with an ACK or NACK result (see
96:  * file header comment for why this differs from the old bit-level
97:  * approach and why synchronous firing is required in this harness).
98:  * ======================================================================== */
99: 
100: typedef enum
101: {
102:   SLAVE_IDLE,
103:   SLAVE_GOT_ADDR,
104:   SLAVE_GOT_REG,
105:   SLAVE_GOT_DATA
106: } slave_state_t;
107: 
108: typedef struct
109: {
110:   slave_state_t state;
111:   bool always_nack;
112:   unsigned int transactions_seen;
113:   unsigned int bytes_seen;
114: } mock_slave_t;
115: 
116: static mock_slave_t g_slave;
117: 
118: static void mock_slave_reset(void)
119: {
120:   memset(&g_slave, 0, sizeof(g_slave));
121:   g_slave.state = SLAVE_IDLE;
122: }
123: 
124: /* Fires the I2C1 ISR with sm_int + ack set/clear as appropriate for the
125:  * byte just "received", advancing g_slave.state.  Called synchronously
126:  * from mock_slave_write_hook() right after each byte is written to
127:  * BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA. */
128: static void mock_slave_ack_and_fire(bool ack)
129: {
130:   uint32_t status = BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT;
131: 
132:   if (ack)
133:     {
134:       status |= BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_ACK;
135:     }
136: 
137:   bk7258_sim_poke32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS, status);
138:   (void)bk7258_sim_irq_fire(BK7258_IRQ_I2C1);
139: }
140: 
141: static void mock_slave_write_hook(uintptr_t addr, uint32_t value, void *arg)
142: {
143:   (void)arg;
144: 
145:   if (addr == BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS &&
146:       (value & BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START) != 0)
147:     {
148:       /* bk7258_i2c1_write_reg() writes the address byte to
149:        * SM_BUS_DATA *before* setting start (matching the real
150:        * hardware's documented write order), so at this point
151:        * SM_BUS_DATA already holds the address byte the driver wants
152:        * to send. */
153:       uint32_t addr_byte = bk7258_sim_peek32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA) &
154:                             BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK;
155: 
156:       g_slave.transactions_seen++;
157:       g_slave.bytes_seen++;
158: 
159:       if (g_slave.always_nack ||
160:           (addr_byte & 0xfeu) != (GC2145_I2C_ADDR_BYTE & 0xfeu))
161:         {
162:           g_slave.state = SLAVE_IDLE;
163:           mock_slave_ack_and_fire(false);
164:           return;
165:         }
166: 
167:       g_slave.state = SLAVE_GOT_ADDR;
168:       mock_slave_ack_and_fire(true);
169:       return;
170:     }
171: 
172:   if (addr != BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA || g_slave.state == SLAVE_IDLE)
173:     {
174:       return;
175:     }
176: 
177:   /* A register-address or data byte write while a transaction is
178:    * already address-ACKed (the driver's ISR writes these from
179:    * BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR/TX_REG_ADDR before this hook can
180:    * observe the *next* sm_int-driven byte -- see bk7258_i2c1.c's ISR:
181:    * it writes the next byte and clears sm_int in the *same* call that
182:    * this write hook is triggered from, so by the time control returns
183:    * here after that inner putreg32(), the byte to ACK is already the
184:    * one just written). */
185:   g_slave.bytes_seen++;
186: 
187:   switch (g_slave.state)
188:     {
189:       case SLAVE_GOT_ADDR:
190:         g_slave.state = SLAVE_GOT_REG;
191:         mock_slave_ack_and_fire(true);
192:         break;
193: 
194:       case SLAVE_GOT_REG:
195:         /* This is the data byte, the last one in a 3-byte write
196:          * transaction: ACK it, then immediately return to IDLE so a
197:          * stray write hook call after the driver's own stop bit write
198:          * (or the very next transaction's address-byte write) is not
199:          * mistaken for a continuation of this already-finished
200:          * transaction. */
201:         g_slave.state = SLAVE_IDLE;
202:         mock_slave_ack_and_fire(true);
203:         break;
204: 
205:       case SLAVE_GOT_DATA:
206:       case SLAVE_IDLE:
207:       default:
208:         break;
209:     }
210: }

text:
## Conclusion

The immediate timeout is caused by an incomplete BK7258 I2C initialization port, not by the GC2145 address or register table.

`int_status=0x00000410` decodes as:

- bit 10 `START` = 1
- bit 4 `RX_FIFO_EMPTY` = 1
- bit 0 `SM_INT` = 0
- bit 1 `SCL_TIMEOUT` = 0
- bit 3 `ARB_LOST` = 0
- bit 14 `MASTER` = 0
- bit 15 `BUSY` = 0

Thus the START command was accepted into the register, but the I2C state machine never entered master-transmit operation. This is earlier than any GC2145 ACK/NACK decision. A wrong address, unpowered sensor, or missing sensor MCLK would produce a completed address phase followed by a NACK/`SM_INT`, not a permanently latched bare START.

`sm_bus_cfg=0xbc001523` is otherwise correct:

- bit 31 `en` = 1
- bit 30 `inh` = 0
- bits 29/28 idle detection and timeout enabled
- bits 27:26 `clk_src` = 3
- bits 15:6 `freq_div` = 84, the expected 26 MHz → approximately 100 kHz divider
- `scl_cr=4`, `idle_cr=3`

## Primary root cause: missing BK7236v5/BK7258 output-mode configuration

The current driver defines the required extended configuration bits but never writes them:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_i2c1.h:72-74`
  - `BK7258_I2C1_EX_DATA_H_OUTEN`, bit 0
  - `BK7258_I2C1_EX_ADDR_H_OUTEN`, bit 1

The current initialization stops after configuring `SM_BUS_CFG`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_i2c1.c:198-230`

In particular, there is no write to `BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_EX_CFG` at `I2C1_BASE + 0x1c`.

The vendor reference explicitly performs both operations for this silicon family:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/i2c_hal.c:60-64`

```c
/* i2c add address/data output mode config in ASIC, since bk7236v5 */
#if (CONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX)
    i2c_ll_enable_addr_output(&hal->hw, hal->id);
    i2c_ll_enable_data_output(&hal->hw, hal->id);
#endif
```

For BK7258, the vendor configuration defines both `CONFIG_SOC_BK7258` and `CONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX`, so that block is compiled. The LL APIs set:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/i2c_ll.h:585-609`
  - `sm_bus_ex_cfg.addr_h_outen = 1`
  - `sm_bus_ex_cfg.data_h_outen = 1`

This behavior also exists in the stable IDK history:

- release/v2.0.1 and release/v2.0.2 use the `CONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX` guard.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/soc/common/hal/i2c_hal.c:59-63` retains the same two APIs under the newer `CONFIG_I2C_DIRECT_DRIVE_MODE` guard.

### Smallest patch for the observed dead START

Insert this after current `bk7258_i2c1.c:220`, before attaching/enabling the IRQ or enabling `SM_BUS_CFG.en`:

```c
modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_EX_CFG, 0,
            BK7258_I2C1_EX_ADDR_H_OUTEN |
            BK7258_I2C1_EX_DATA_H_OUTEN);
```

Equivalent vendor APIs are:

```c
i2c_ll_enable_addr_output(...);
i2c_ll_enable_data_output(...);
```

The expected `SM_BUS_EX_CFG` low bits after initialization are therefore `0x00000003`.

This is the minimum change that addresses the exact `0x410` signature.

## Second I2C defect: interrupt-status writes do not follow the vendor handshake

Once the state machine starts, the current ISR has another concrete mismatch that can prevent a complete three-byte write.

Current code treats `SM_INT` as a write-one-to-clear bit:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_i2c1.c:124`
- same file: `134`, `141`, `148`

```c
putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
```

The vendor does the opposite. Its status-commit operation clears bit 0 in the value written:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/i2c_ll.h:504-516`

```c
if (int_status & I2C1_F_SM_INT) {
    int_status &= ~I2C1_F_SM_INT;
}
REG_WRITE(I2C1_R_INT_STAUS, int_status);
```

The vendor ISR also clears the latched START command from its status shadow before committing it:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c:1032-1045`

```c
s_i2c[id].int_status &= ~I2C1_F_START;
...
i2c_hal_clear_interrupt_status(hal, s_i2c[id].int_status);
```

The important vendor comment is at:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c:1111-1115`

It says `sm_int/ack/start/stop/int_mode` must be operated in one full status-register write. The current port instead issues isolated writes, and `bk7258_i2c1_stop()` writes `SM_INT|STOP` followed by another isolated `SM_INT` write.

### Minimal vendor-consistent status helper

Add a helper conceptually equivalent to:

```c
static void bk7258_i2c1_commit_status(uint32_t status)
{
  status &= ~(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT |
              BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START);
  putreg32(status, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
}
```

Then:

- At current lines 134 and 141, replace the isolated `SM_INT` write with:

```c
bk7258_i2c1_commit_status(int_status);
```

- For NACK and final-data completion, issue STOP in the same commit:

```c
bk7258_i2c1_commit_status(int_status |
                          BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_STOP);
```

- Remove the extra writes at current lines 124 and 148.
- `bk7258_i2c1_stop()` should accept the status snapshot or otherwise construct one full outgoing status value; it should not independently write `SM_INT|STOP`.

For subsequent transactions, the START command should also follow the vendor’s `disable_stop()` → write address → `enable_start()` ordering. At minimum, replace current line 274 with a modification that clears stale STOP while setting START:

```c
modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS,
            BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_STOP,
            BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START);
```

This ISR defect is not what created the initial `0x410`—there was no `SM_INT` to service—but it should be corrected with the output-mode patch or the transaction may stall as soon as its first real interrupt arrives. The existing simulation does not detect this because its write hook fabricates and recursively fires each ACK interrupt when `SM_BUS_DATA` is written.

## Camera-side defect that will appear next: MCLK is not enabled

Both current GC2145 implementations only select a GPIO27 function; neither enables the sensor’s 24 MHz input clock:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc2145.c:773-785`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_camera_imgsensor.c:820-832`

They currently use function index 0 for GPIO27. Vendor camera bring-up instead maps GPIO27 to `GPIO_DEV_CLK_AUXS_CIS`, which is function index 1:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:55`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_dvp/src/dvp_common.c:28-32`

The vendor then programs and enables 24 MHz before initializing I2C:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_dvp/src/dvp_common.c:48-50`
- same file: `69`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_dvp/src/bk_dvp.c:1511-1517`

```c
gpio_dev_map(GPIO_27, GPIO_DEV_CLK_AUXS_CIS);
sys_drv_set_auxs_cis(3, 19);   /* 24 MHz */
sys_drv_set_cis_auxs_clk_en(1);
bk_i2c_init(...);
```

### Minimal camera patch

In both current camera drivers:

1. Give MCLK its own function index:

```c
#define DVP_MCLK_PINMUX_FUNCTION 1u
```

and use it only for GPIO27; PCLK/HSYNC/VSYNC/data remain function index 0.

2. Before `bk7258_i2c1_init()`, perform the equivalent of:

```c
sys_drv_set_auxs_cis(3, 19);
sys_drv_set_cis_auxs_clk_en(1);
```

If implemented directly through registers, the exact BK7258 fields are:

- `0x44010028`
  - bits 16:15 `cksel_auxs_cis = 3`
  - bits 21:17 `ckdiv_auxs_cis = 19`
  - mask `0x003f8000`
  - value `0x00278000`
- `0x44010034`
  - bit 9 `cis_auxs_cken = 1`, value `0x00000200`

This missing MCLK is not responsible for the current bare-START timeout, but after I2C itself is fixed it can cause the GC2145 to NACK address `0x3c`.

## Items that are already correct

- GC2145 address `0x3c` is correct:
  - current `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc2145.c:41-45`

  - system clock-enable register `0x44010030`, bit 8.

  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_irq.c:145-157`
